sourceFull: Data: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, reply to Parliament (2024 figures)

parts: In twenty twenty-four, potholes killed two thousand three hundred and eighty-five people on India's roads.
That's more than six people, every single day.
The sudden jolt. The swerve. The held breath.
It's rain, heavy loads, rushed repairs, and roads dug up again and again by crews who never talk.
Every city on Earth fights the same battle between water, weight and time.
What if roads could report their own damage, before it became a hole?
Repairs planned by need, not by noise.
Every job, its cost and its quality, open for anyone to check.
Intelligence like A.L.K.I. could help plan it.
OmniChain is designed to keep that record honest.
And OmniBot is being built to take on the heavy, dangerous work.
It takes engineers, contractors, citizens, and the people who run our cities, working from the same truth.
One hand can't lift a road. A thousand hands can.
Six lives a day. Let's build roads that bring everyone home.
